root_cause.text: The vulnerability arises from concurrent read-modify-write operations on bitfields sharing the same underlying storage unit within the `mmc_host` structure, allowing unrelated flag updates to overwrite each other during asynchronous execution.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "The host->claimed bit shared a word with retune flags" and writes "can overwrite other bits when concurrent updates happen in other contexts," while the patch resolves this by converting `claimed`, `can_retune`, `retune_now`, and `retune_paused` from packed bitfields to separate `bool` declarations to remove shared-word coupling.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the MMC core `struct mmc_host`, packing the `claimed` and retune control flags into a shared bitfield word caused non-atomic Read-Modify-Write operations that corrupted unrelated flags during concurrent asynchronous updates.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch converts `claimed`, `can_retune`, `retune_now`, and `retune_paused` from bitfields to `bool` types to remove shared-word coupling, explicitly stating that concurrent writes to one flag could overwrite bits belonging to others in the same word, triggering spurious warnings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extends struct mmc_host with new boolean flags to manage SD card re-tuning states and execution control.
intent_record.what: Added three boolean fields (can_retune, retune_now, retune_paused) to the struct mmc_host definition.
intent_record.how: Enables the MMC subsystem to track re-tuning capabilities, request immediate re-tuning, and temporarily suspend re-tuning operations.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is part of the mmc_host structure where bitfields share the same underlying storage unit. When multiple 1-bit flags are packed into the same storage allocation, concurrent read-modify-write operations can cause unrelated flag updates to overwrite each other during asynchronous execution, creating a race condition vulnerability.

This adjacent field declaration contributes to the storage unit packing issue. When combined with other bitfields in the structure, these declarations create conditions where concurrent modifications to different flags can interfere with each other due to shared underlying storage.

anchors: unsigned int		claimed:1;	/* host exclusively claimed */
unsigned int		can_retune:1;	/* re-tuning can be used */
unsigned int		retune_now:1;	/* do re-tuning at next req */
